eras.label: 1000–1100 CE · western and south-central Kentucky
eras.text:
Mississippian is an archaeological culture, a group of sites that archaeologists define from the pottery, village layouts and dates they share; it is not a tribe, and no descent from or link to any later people is claimed. The Kentucky Archaeological Survey dates the Mississippi period to about AD 1000–1700 and covers the Purchase, Green River and Upper Cumberland regions and part of the Salt River region. The tint is eight whole Kentucky counties named for documented towns and mound centers (Ballard, Carlisle, Fulton, Marshall, Crittenden, Butler, Logan, Knox). The chapter gives no county list for the culture, so this is a general area, not a boundary, and it is drawn for these site counties only. Dated site dots use each story's public map pin, rounded, not the exact location.

Dated sites on the map in this span (occupation years from each site story's cited source): Jonathan Creek Mississippian center (1000–1300 CE); Page Site / “Lost City” (15LO1) (1000–1100 CE).
